title: The Hunter and the Woodman
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Hunter was searching in the forest for the tracks of a lion, and, catching sight presently of a Woodman engaged in felling a tree, he went up to him and asked him if he had noticed a lion's footprints anywhere about, or if he knew where his den was. The Woodman answered, "If you will come with me, I will show you the lion himself." The Hunter turned pale with fear, and his teeth chattered as he replied, "Oh, I'm not looking for the lion, thanks, but only for his tracks."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Hunter searching for in the forest?
options: The tracks of a lion
A lost hunting dog
A stream to drink from
A place to build a shelter

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Woodman doing when the Hunter caught sight of him?
options: Felling a tree
Resting beside a stream
Gathering berries
Building a fire

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two things did the Hunter ask the Woodman about?
options: Whether he had seen a lion's footprints, and if he knew where its den was
Whether the forest was safe, and how far it stretched
Whether he had seen other hunters, and where they had gone
Whether he needed help felling the tree, and how long it would take

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Woodman offer to do?
options: Show the Hunter the lion himself
Lend the Hunter his axe
Point the Hunter toward the nearest village
Help the Hunter track the lion's footprints

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Hunter's body react to the Woodman's offer?
options: He turned pale with fear, and his teeth chattered
He laughed and thanked the Woodman warmly
He raised his weapon eagerly
He fainted on the spot

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hunter say he is actually looking for?
options: Only the lion's tracks, not the lion himself
A guide who knows the whole forest
A safer path out of the woods
Another hunter to join him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Hunter's reaction reveal about his true courage?
options: He is far less brave than his search for the lion's tracks made him appear
He is braver than the Woodman gives him credit for
He is only afraid of lions specifically, not other dangers
He was simply startled by the Woodman's sudden offer, not truly afraid

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It is easy to claim boldness when the real danger is not actually at hand
Woodmen know the forest better than any hunter ever could
Lions are more dangerous when encountered unexpectedly
Hunters should always travel with a companion for safety

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in what setting does the Hunter meet the Woodman?
options: In the forest
On a mountain road
By a riverbank
In a village square

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hunter ask about the lion's den?
options: Whether the Woodman knew where it was
Whether the Woodman had ever been inside it
How far it was from the village
How many lions lived there

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition does the Woodman set for showing the Hunter the lion?
options: That the Hunter come with him
That the Hunter first pay him a fee
That the Hunter wait until morning
That the Hunter bring more men

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Hunter suddenly change what he says he wants?
options: The prospect of actually facing the lion terrifies him, unlike merely tracking it
He realizes the Woodman is lying about knowing the lion's location
He decides tracking is more sporting than a direct encounter
He no longer trusts the Woodman to guide him safely

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "chattered" mean in "his teeth chattered"?
options: Rattled together rapidly, as from fear or cold
Spoke rapidly and cheerfully
Ground together in anger
Fell out one by one

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Hunter asks about a lion's tracks, but grows terrified when the Woodman offers to show him the actual lion
The Woodman refuses to help the Hunter find any trace of the lion
The Hunter and Woodman together track down and confront the lion
The Woodman mistakes the Hunter for another lion hunter he had met before
